### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /profile — 1cr

Returns a unified Facebook Author profile with page ID, display name, profile URL, profile image, bio (the page intro), follower count, page-like count, and creation date. A **business page** carries considerably more than a personal profile, and all of it rides in `author.ext`: `business_category`, `website`, `links[]`, `public_phone`, `public_email`, `address`, `price_range`, `rating` (Facebook's recommendation string) with `rating_count`, `talking_about_count`, `cover_url`, `page_active`, and `ad_library_page_id` / `ad_library_status` — the Ad Library page id is a different id from `author.id` and is the one `/v1/facebook/adlibrary/company/ads` takes, so you can chain profile → ads off a single lookup. A personal profile returns null for the listing fields it has no equivalent for rather than omitting them. `links[]` and `business_hours[]` are also mapped, the latter only when you pass `get_business_hours=true`, but Facebook returned both empty on every page measured on 2026-08-11, so treat them as best effort rather than data you can depend on. `author.following` and `author.posts_count` remain null because the upstream profile response does not provide those totals.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Facebook page or profile
- `get_business_hours` *(optional)*: Get the business's hours

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/posts — 1cr

Returns a list of recent posts from a Facebook page or profile. Each post includes the post text, like count, comment count, share count, media attachments, and publish timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `cursor` *(optional)*: To paginate through the posts
- `url` / `pageId` — at least one required.
  - `url`: Full URL of the Facebook page or profile to fetch posts for (one of: url, pageId — at least one required)
  - `pageId`: Facebook profile page id (one of: url, pageId — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile/posts?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post — 1cr

Returns detailed information about a specific Facebook post including the post text, like count, comment count, share count, reactions breakdown, media attachments, and author info.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Facebook post
- `get_comments` *(optional)*: Whether you want to get the first several comments of the post
- `get_transcript` *(optional)*: Whether you want to get the transcript of the post

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/post?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post/comments — 1cr

Returns a list of comments on a specific Facebook post. Each comment includes the author name, comment text, like count, reply count, and creation timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to get more comments. Get 'cursor' from previous response.
- `url` / `feedback_id` — at least one required.
  - `url`: Full URL of the Facebook post to fetch comments for (one of: url, feedback_id — at least one required)
  - `feedback_id`: Using feedback_id (instead of url) will *really* speed up the request. You can get the feedback_id when you make a request to /v1/facebook/post. (one of: url, feedback_id — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/post/comments?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /group/posts — 1cr

Returns recent posts from a Facebook group. Each post includes text, reaction count, comment count, shares, and author info. Pagination is not currently supported on this endpoint — the upstream returns a single page only.

**Parameters**

- `sort_by` *(optional)*: How to sort the posts
- `url` / `group_id` — at least one required.
  - `url`: Full URL of the Facebook group (one of: url, group_id — at least one required)
  - `group_id`: The ID of the group (one of: url, group_id — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/group/posts?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Returns the transcript of a Facebook video post. Supports auto-generated captions.

```bash

  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/photos — 1cr

Returns Facebook page or profile photos as unified Post items. Each item includes a photo ID, permalink, full-size image URL, thumbnail, and accessibility caption when available. Per-item author, engagement counts, and publish time are not exposed, so those canonical fields and engagement counts remain null.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Facebook page or profile
- `next_page_id` *(optional)*: To paginate through to the next page Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: To paginate through to the next page

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile/photos?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/reels — 1cr

Returns Facebook page or profile reels as unified Post items. Each item includes a reel ID, description, thumbnail, duration when available, author identity, `engagement.views` when the upstream provides it, permalink, and publish time. Likes, comments, shares, and saves remain null because this endpoint does not expose those counts. **Two caveats worth knowing before you grade on these numbers:** (1) `engagement.views` here is Facebook's ROUNDED public display value (the "12K" / "2.6M" the page shows, parsed back to a number — e.g. 12000 where the true count is 12366), not an exact count; (2) the upstream carries no per-reel engagement beyond that view count. For EXACT views plus likes, comments, and shares, the easiest path is `GET /v1/facebook/profile/reels/full`, which runs this list and the per-reel lookups server-side and merges the exact engagement in (flat 5 credits per page of 10 reels). Alternatively, take each item's `post.url` and pass it to `/v1/facebook/post` (single) or batch up to 100 of them into `POST /v1/prism/post-stats` (1 credit per successful URL, dead links refunded).

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Facebook page or profile
- `next_page_id` *(optional)*: To paginate through to the next page Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: To paginate through to the next page

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile/reels?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adlibrary/ad — 5cr

Returns detailed information about a specific ad from the Facebook Ad Library — creative, spend, impressions, and targeting. For ad video transcripts, use `/v1/facebook/adlibrary/ad/transcript` (separate endpoint, premium tier).

**Parameters**

- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true for a trimmed down version of the response
- `id` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `id`: Facebook Ad Library ad ID (one of: id, url — at least one required)
  - `url`: Facebook Ad URL (one of: id, url — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/adlibrary/ad?id=<id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adlibrary/company/ads — 5cr

Returns ads from a specific company/page in the Facebook Ad Library. Each ad includes creative, status, spend, and targeting info.

**Parameters**

- `country` *(optional)*: This can only be one country. It has to be the 2 letter code for the country. It defaults to ALL.
- `status` *(optional)*: Status of the ad. Defaults to ACTIVE.
- `media_type` *(optional)*: Media type of the ad. Defaults to ALL. Meme refers to ads with image and text. Not sure why they call it meme.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language to filter ads on. Needs to be 2 letter language code, ie EN, ES, FR, etc
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Sort by impressions (high to low), or Most Recent (relevancy_monthly_grouped). Defaults to impressions.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Start date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `end_date` *(optional)*: End date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to paginate through results
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true for a trimmed down version of the response
- `pageId` / `companyName` — at least one required.
  - `pageId`: Facebook page ID of the advertiser (one of: pageId, companyName — at least one required)
  - `companyName`: The name of the company. Can either use this or pageId (one of: pageId, companyName — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/adlibrary/company/ads?pageId=<pageId>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adlibrary/search/ads — 5cr

Searches the Facebook Ad Library for ads matching a keyword. Returns matching ads with creative text, images, sponsor info, and status.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword or phrase to find ads in the Facebook Ad Library
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Sort by impressions (high to low), or Most Recent (relevancy_monthly_grouped). Defaults to impressions.
- `search_type` *(optional)*: If you want to search by exact phrase or not
- `ad_type` *(optional)*: Search for all ads or only political and issue ads
- `country` *(optional)*: This can only be one country. It has to be the 2 letter code for the country. It defaults to ALL.
- `status` *(optional)*: Status of the ad. Defaults to ACTIVE.
- `media_type` *(optional)*: Media type of the ad. Defaults to ALL. Meme just means the ad has text and an image. No clue why they call it meme.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Impressions start date. Needs to be in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- `end_date` *(optional)*: Impressions end date. Needs to be in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to paginate through results
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true for a trimmed down version of the response

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/adlibrary/search/ads?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post/comment/replies — 1cr

Returns the reply thread for a single Facebook comment. Both `feedback_id` and `expansion_token` come from the parent `/v1/facebook/post/comments` response — note that `feedback_id` is NOT the comment ID. Forward the returned cursor for additional pages.

**Parameters**

- `feedback_id`: `feedback_id` from `/v1/facebook/post/comments` for the parent comment (this is NOT the comment ID).
- `expansion_token`: `expansion_token` from `/v1/facebook/post/comments` for the parent comment.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor returned by the previous response for pagination.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/post/comment/replies?feedback_id=<feedback_id>&expansion_token=<expansion_token>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /marketplace/location/search — 1cr

Searches Facebook Marketplace locations and cities, returning lat/lng coordinates you can feed into `/v1/facebook/marketplace/search`.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Location search query (city or area name).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/marketplace/location/search?query=<query>" \
```

### /marketplace/search — 1cr

Searches Facebook Marketplace listings by keyword + lat/lng with price, condition, delivery, and date-listed filters. Forward the returned cursor for additional pages. With `sort_by=creation_time_descend`, FB may return slightly different ordering across identical requests — for alerting workflows, scrape multiple pages and dedupe by listing id rather than assuming stable order.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword (e.g., `bike`, `couch`).
- `lat`: Latitude of the search location.
- `lng`: Longitude of the search location.
- `radius_km` *(optional)*: Search radius in kilometers.
- `min_price` *(optional)*: Minimum listing price.
- `max_price` *(optional)*: Maximum listing price.
- `count` *(optional)*: Number of listings to return per page. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Sort order for results.
- `delivery_method` *(optional)*: Delivery filter — local pickup only, shipping only, or all.
- `condition` *(optional)*: Filter listings by item condition.
- `date_listed` *(optional)*: Filter by listing recency (relative window or numeric day count).
- `availability` *(optional)*: Filter by listing status — `available`, `sold`, or `all`.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous response — forward as-is.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `count`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/marketplace/search?query=<query>&lat=<lat>&lng=<lng>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adlibrary/ad/transcript — 10cr

Retrieves a transcript for a single Facebook Ad Library video ad. Uses Facebook-provided captions when available, otherwise transcribes the public video URL on demand. Ads without retrievable captions return a 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, and on-demand transcription can fail transiently (503) — both outcomes are free; credits are only deducted when a transcript is returned.

> ⛔ **BANNED in this plugin: 10 credits, no advantage. Transcribe with the local captions→Groq→Whisper chain instead.**

**Parameters**

- `id` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `id`: Facebook Ad Library ad ID. (one of: id, url — at least one required)
  - `url`: Facebook Ad Library ad URL. (one of: id, url — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/adlibrary/ad/transcript?id=<id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/full — 5cr

Fans out to the Facebook profile and recent-posts endpoints in parallel and returns the unified author, the recent-post list, and computed metrics: average engagement rate, posting cadence (with the window it was measured over), the top post, and the format mix. The profile leg is the only critical leg: if posts can't be fetched the call still returns the profile with post-dependent metrics null, and every leg's status is surfaced in legs[]. Flat 5 credits. For Facebook, `author.following` and `author.posts_count` remain null because the profile upstream does not provide those totals.

**Parameters**

- `url` *(optional)*: url
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many recent posts to fetch + average the computed metrics over (1–100, default 25).
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Pass a prior response's posts_cursor to deepen the post window.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of posts,computed (default both). include=computed drops the raw posts[] to save payload.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile/full" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/reels/full — 5cr per page of 10 reels

Returns a Facebook page or profile's reels with EXACT per-reel engagement merged in — one call instead of the reels-list → post-stats chain. The plain `/v1/facebook/profile/reels` list only carries a rounded public view count ("12K" parsed back to 12000) and no likes, comments, or shares, because Facebook exposes those on the individual reel permalink only. This endpoint fetches the list, then queries each reel's permalink server-side and overwrites the item's `engagement` with the exact figures: `views` (the rounded list value is replaced), `likes`, `comments`, and `shares`. `saves` stays null (Facebook exposes no public save count), and `comments` can be null on a zero-comment reel (a quirk of the permalink upstream). Per-item `ext.engagement_source` is `"post_detail"` when the exact figures landed and null when that reel's lookup failed (the item then keeps the honest list values); read `engagement_coverage` before grading, and `_warnings: ["engagement_partial"]` flags a partial page. Billing: a flat 5 credits per page of 10 reels (1 credit for the list + 4 for the per-reel enrichment, roughly half the cost of running the chain yourself); if enrichment yields zero coverage the 4-credit premium is refunded automatically. Paginate with `next_cursor`, or pass `limit` (1–50) to have the endpoint walk pages server-side until it has collected that many reels, billed per page consumed.

> ⚠️ **Metered per page of 10 reels — the 5cr figure is a UNIT price, not the price of the request.** limit=50 = 25cr. Multiply by the number of page of 10 reelss you send before calling; only successful units are charged.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Facebook page or profile
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor from a prior response's next_cursor to page deeper.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Return up to this many reels in one call (1–50). The endpoint pages the underlying list server-side until it has collected this many (or runs out), and bills per upstream page consumed (5 credits/page of 10). If the walk hits the internal time budget first, the response carries `_warnings: ["walk_deadline_reached"]`, unfetched pages are refunded, and `next_cursor` resumes where it stopped. Omit for a single page.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/facebook/profile/reels/full?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Facebook endpoint

Two very different things live here: ordinary page/profile data at 1cr, and the **Ad Library**
at 5cr. The Ad Library is the reason most research reaches for Facebook at all.

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Page profile / its posts / one post | `/profile` · `/profile/posts` · `/post` | 1 |
| Comments, and replies to a comment | `/post/comments` · `/post/comment/replies` | 1 |
| Photos, reels, events for a page | `/profile/photos` · `/profile/reels` · `/profile/events` | 1 |
| Group posts | `/group/posts` | 1 |
| Marketplace search / one item / locations | `/marketplace/search` · `/marketplace/item` · `/marketplace/location/search` | 1 |
| Events by keyword or city | `/events/search` · `/events` · `/event/details` | 1 |
| **What ads is this company running?** | `/adlibrary/company/ads` | 5 |
| Find the advertiser first | `/adlibrary/search/companies` | 5 |
| Search ad creatives by keyword | `/adlibrary/search/ads` | 5 |
| One ad's full detail | `/adlibrary/ad` | 5 |
| Profile + posts + analytics in one call | `/profile/full` | 5 |
| Reels with exact views/likes/comments/shares | `/profile/reels/full` | 5 |
| ~~Transcripts~~ | ⛔ `/post/transcript`, `/adlibrary/ad/transcript` **banned** | — |

### The Ad Library is a competitor's paid strategy, stated openly

`/adlibrary/company/ads` (5cr) returns the ads a company is actively running — their claims,
their offers, their hooks, and how long each has been live. A creative that has run for months
is one they are still paying for, which is the closest thing to seeing a competitor's test
results. Budget 10cr for the usual two-step: `/adlibrary/search/companies` to resolve the
advertiser, then `/adlibrary/company/ads` to pull the creatives.

Compare with `google/company/ads` (5cr) for search-side advertising and
`linkedin/ads/search` (5cr) for B2B.

### Facebook's `profile` is thinner than other platforms'

It supplies follower and page-like counts but not following or total-post counts. That is an
upstream limitation, not a missing parameter — do not spend a second call hunting for them.

## Field Maps


The `profile` endpoint returns an `Author` response normalized by the `facebook-author` field map, and `post` returns a `Post` normalized by `facebook-post`. Both include computed fields under `data.computed`. Use `?format=raw` to bypass both. Other Facebook endpoints are passthrough.
